subject: Session boundaries, auto-purge schedule, and EU residency — BrightBank follow-up
messages:
From: Sam Carter <sam.carter@brightbank.com>
To: avery.johnson@redwood.ai
Cc: security@brightbank.com
Date: 2026-11-16T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Quick clarifications on what persists after a session closes

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Two quick follow-ups from our security team: when a user finishes a session (e.g., a chat or single request), what exactly persists by default in your hosted product? Specifically they asked about:
- the raw request and raw model response (full text)
- any intermediate derivatives (summaries, embeddings, re-ranked candidates)
- session-level state like KV cache and tool-call traces

Also important for us: if the account is created in the EU region, does data ever move outside the EU for default logging?

We're just trying to map what we need to request in our procurement wording. Appreciate a clear, short bullet list we can include in our Security Questionnaire.

Best,
Sam
Sam Carter
Senior InfoSec Manager, BrightBank
Attachment: security-questionnaire-v3.xlsx (xls)

From: avery.johnson@redwood.ai
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@brightbank.com>
Cc: security@brightbank.com, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-16T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Quick clarifications on what persists after a session closes

Sam — thanks for the concise list, and great questions. I pulled together a short answer and attached a one‑page summary. High level: defaults are conservative but configurable. Key points below, then Marissa and Karthik have added a couple of product/legal clarifications in follow‑ups.

Bulleted defaults (hosted Redwood API):
- Raw requests and direct model outputs: retained by default for 30 days for operational diagnostics and quality checks, then deleted automatically unless the customer opts into longer retention.
- Derivatives (embeddings, reranks, generated summaries): stored by default for 90 days; these are used for caching and workload optimization.
- Session KV cache (in-memory) & transient streaming buffers: not persisted to long‑term storage; cache entries are ephemeral and dropped at session end or after 1 hour of inactivity.
- Tool-calls / structured tool outputs: logged to audit store and retained for 180 days by default to support troubleshooting and compliance reviews.

Residency note: If a customer selects the EU region for hosted accounts, default logs and artifacts are kept within EU storage (Ireland) and are not replicated outside the EU for the default logging pipeline. Certain backend metadata (service metrics, aggregated telemetry) may be processed in our control plane in the US but never includes identifiable request/response content.

Deletion paths: customers can request immediate purge via the Console (Data > Purge) or through our API; purge requests trigger asynchronous deletion across caches and stores and we provide an audit record. We also support scheduled auto‑purge policies the customer can set to shorten the default windows.

Attachment: redwood-retention-summary-202611.pdf (pdf) — one pager with the windows above and a diagram.

— Avery
Avery Johnson
Enterprise Solutions (Sales Engineering)
Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Subject: RE: Quick clarifications on what persists after a session closes

Adding a couple of product clarifications for your procurement language, Sam. Short answers you can paste into the questionnaire:

1) "Default retention windows (hosted): requests/responses = 30 days; derivatives = 90 days; tool/audit logs = 180 days; aggregated telemetry = 365 days (non-identifiable)."
2) "Data residency: When EU region is selected, request/response and derivative stores are provisioned in-region and are not replicated to other regions by default. Customers can opt into cross-region replication for DR — that requires explicit config and contractual approval."
3) "Deletion guarantees: Purge requests are propagated to long-term stores within 48 hours and to short-term caches within minutes. We provide deletion confirmation and an audit log entry for compliance. Note: backups and cold archives have separate retention — we expedite their purging on contractual commitments (enterprise customers)."

One nuance: embeddings used for customer indexing are classified as 'derivatives' and are deleted per the derivative window unless the customer requests a longer archival policy. If BrightBank requires an absolute non-retention option for derivatives, our Dedicated/Private options allow a locked-down config where those artifacts are not persisted.

— Marissa
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@brightbank.com>, avery.johnson@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai

Subject: RE: Quick clarifications on what persists after a session closes

Sam — two operational points to call out that often get missed in questionnaire answers:

- KV cache vs. persistent store: we never materialize the KV cache into the persistent logging tier in hosted-by-default configurations. That cache is an optimization for inference and is dropped at session termination. If your deployment uses Dedicated capacity with a customer-managed cache persistence option, that becomes part of your scope.

- Auditability & proof of deletion: when a purge runs we emit a deletion event id and a job record. For enterprise contracts we support an annual attestation and one-off verification requests where our compliance team will provide a deletion manifest for a given timeframe.

If BrightBank needs the wording tightened up for SOW language, happy to draft suggested clauses.

— Karthik
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
